findings: All four observed original unauthenticated reads returned from data(from:delegate:) with final HTTP403 and131 body bytes. No observed request threw or lacked a metric callback.
The negative-read timeout did not recur in this diagnostic run. This does not resolve previous Apple or Windows failures.
All final transactions reported http/1.1, no proxy and no redirect; three final transactions reused a connection and auth did not. All four final transactions supplied response start/end times.

Health and auth each reported two transaction observations. The first had status200, raw resourceFetchType3 and zero wire/decoded body counters; final403/body receipt is the caller outcome. This report makes no claim that an intermediate cached-looking response was returned to the unauthenticated caller.
Callback-to-terminal monotonic intervals range0.136–8.727ms in these successful observations; this is not evidence about the earlier failing task.

Observer intervals are wider than a pure data-await interval: started() emits synchronously before invoking data(), and terminal timestamps precede synchronous output after data() returns. No I/O runs inside didFinishCollecting.

timingQualification.interpretation: These gaps can include diagnostic output and caller scheduling. The current metrics do not time FileHandle.write separately or establish a specific blocked sink, queue or socket.

betweenHealthEndAndAuthStartStatements.statement: Health end is timestamped in emit(); afterward it adds scalar fields, converts the copied metric snapshot to JSON, builds the line and synchronously calls FileHandle.standardError.write(contentsOf: line).
finished() returns; observedRuntimeDeniedRead returns the already completed Data/URLResponse and executes its withExtendedLifetime defer.
The caller checks the completed health response status with the original XCTAssertEqual and advances the original for-loop from health to auth.
The next helper constructs a fresh observer and calls started(), with no intervening data request in this source path.
The auth start emit snapshots its fresh bounded state and captures the next timestamp.

authStartToTaskTimingStatements.statement: The auth start timestamp precedes JSON encoding and synchronous diagnostic output; only after started() returns does the helper invoke URLSession.shared.data(from:delegate:).

timingQualification.qualification: The source has no data await between those two observation timestamps. It does have synchronous diagnostic I/O plus assertion/loop/observer work, and execution can be descheduled. There is no separate duration measurement of those operations, so a blocked logging sink or scheduling delay remains an inference, not an established cause.
